column1: # The ways PDFium's tests open the encrypted PDFs of its testing/resources, one
# line for each way of opening one file, read from the test sources named above
# each group. fetch-corpus.ps1 writes these lines to _passwords.tsv with the
# suite's name in front of each file.
# A line gives a password the test source holds, and an empty one besides where
# the file also opens with none. Ten of the 341 files name an encryption
# dictionary; every one of them is here.
# **On the two encodings.** PDFium tests each of these passwords twice, once as
# UTF-8 bytes and once as Latin-1 -- kAgeUTF8 is "\xc3\xa2ge" and kAgeLatin1
# "\xe2ge", the same "age" with a circumflex on the a. A password here is a
# string and not a byte sequence, because that is what both PDFBox and the port
# take, and each of them encodes it the way the revision asks: ISO-8859-1 for
# revisions 2 to 4, UTF-8 for 5 and 6. So one line covers both of PDFium's
# cases, and the Latin-1 byte sequence on its own is not writable in a UTF-8
# table anyway.
# core/fpdfapi/parser/cpdf_security_handler_embeddertest.cpp, UserPassword and
# OwnerPassword: RC4, opened with the user password and with the owner's.
# NoPassword and BadPassword expect no password and "tiger" to fail.
